key_insight: A symmetric semi-implicit projection scheme achieves second-order time accuracy for spherical shallow-water equations while restricting stability by advection rather than fast waves.
engineering_relevance: The method supports larger time steps for geophysical flow simulations by subcycling advection without adding implicit wave solves.
method: Use compatible finite elements with DG-upwind SSPRK3 advection.
Apply an explicit half-step, full advection step, and implicit half-step that projects velocity into H(div).
Solve the implicit wave system efficiently through hybridisation in Firedrake.
evidence_signal: Standard spherical shallow-water benchmarks demonstrate second-order convergence, good parallel scaling, and stable results at Courant numbers up to 1 with two advection subcycles and second-order finite elements.
watch_item: Advection remains CFL-limited; larger overall time steps require subcycling, which adds explicit computational work.
paper_title: A Second-Order Semi-Implicit Projection Time-Stepping Scheme for the Shallow-Water Equations on the Sphere Using Compatible Finite Elements
